Requirement changes and regression tests

Unit 3 · Week 1 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Use the Unit 3 Week 1 student workbook and separate public teacher key at slides/practice/u3-week1/. Download the companion ZIP; extract before running. Python 3; Lesson 2 additionally uses the existing pygame/pygame-teaching-pack.zip and its pinned requirements. Read the unit3-fluency chapter and foundations workbook. Use fictional values and disposable history files only. No extra assessment or homework. Suggested 55-minute plans are untrialled; select one repair rather than completing every extension.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Week 1 practical resources

Follow the slide order; preserve each unaided response before opening its feedback.

Student workbook · Separate public teacher key · Download practical files · Four editable decks and resources

1. Requirement changes and regression tests

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Retain existing lesson scope: linear/iterative comparison, requirement change and transfer test. Consolidate syntax/runtime/logic diagnosis while revising a small Python rule. No new assessment or project features.

2. Retrieval: three kinds of fault

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Closed-note retrieval

Ask for predictions first. SyntaxError at parsing; ValueError when executed; logic fault produces wrong result. Use fresh small examples if these have already been seen. Students identify stage, cause and minimal failing input; avoid equating all exceptions with syntax errors.

3. Two ways to organise development

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Explicit comparison and discussion

Explain investigate/analyse/design/develop/implement/evaluate in the chapter’s terms. A linear process can authorise a documented return when requirements change; it is not incapable of change. Iteration still needs a plan and acceptance criteria. Ask pairs which approach suits stable versus evolving rules, and what the cost of rework is. Do not claim one process is universally best.

4. The changed requirement is precise

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked requirement-to-test model

Record change C01,reason,boundary and affected predicate. Old expected3; new expected2. Update requirement/design/implementation/test expectations together. Show the parameterised function in the workbook after predictions. A syntax fault, runtime conversion or wrong > predicate needs different evidence, not random edits.

5. Guided repair and regression

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided test design

Use workbook C01. For threshold6: [5]=0,[6]=1,[7]=1,[]=0,[6,6]=2. Recheck threshold5 call [4,5,7]=2 in parameterised function: previously valid behaviour remains supported. If restoring old logic simply to pass old expectations, distinguish changed requirements from regression. Teacher models one test then fades the remaining expected column.

6. A fresh requirement, independently

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent transfer and optional extension

Close model. [7,8,9,8]=>3,[]=0,[8,8]=>2. Write count_at_least(values,minimum), then run checks, record help and retain original attempt. Optional secure-learner extension: specify a policy for nonnumeric input and justify where validation belongs; do not silently add it to common requirements.

7. Peer moderation of the explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Peer critique

Use key only after preserving the independent solution. Partner asks which evidence establishes the boundary and which case protects unchanged behaviour. Explain iterative revisit of design/build/test and controlled linear return with updated documents. A passing sample is not proof of absence of faults.

8. Exit: a client changes the threshold

Suggested time: 3 minutes

Instructional strategy: Exit ticket

Allocated u3-l3. Expected: iteration revisits design/build/test; linear may need a controlled return; retest previously valid behaviour. If iterative is described as no planning, ask for documented revision and acceptance criteria. Record an unresolved fault for later retrieval.
